report.summary: Reviewed chunk 2 of subprocess_adapter.py (lines 281-393). Contains stream, parse_line, parse_typed_event, approve, reject, interrupt, _stop_process, terminate. No docstrings; comments make checkable claims.
risks: line 290 | medium | yield started before checking remaining timeout; if timeout already expired the while loop will immediately raise TimeoutError, but started was already published and yielded. | Verify if publishing a SessionStarted event before timeout check is intentional or could cause inconsistent state.

line 303 | medium | on asyncio.TimeoutError, _stop_process is called then TimeoutError re-raised; but the exception is caught after wait_for, so the process may already have been stopped by the timeout. | Confirm that double stop is harmless.
line 312 | medium | session.stderr_task is awaited after process.wait; if stderr_task has an exception it may raise. | Ensure stderr_task is robust or errors are handled.
line 316 | low | stderr is truncated to last 4000 chars; could lose important error context. | Consider if full stderr is needed elsewhere.
line 326 | low | _parse_line returns TextDelta(text=line) for non-JSON lines; but line is already stripped of newline and may be empty (empty lines are skipped earlier). | No issue.

line 348 | medium | _parse_typed_event for event_type 'assistant' constructs AgentMessage from concatenated text blocks; but if no text blocks, falls back to TextDelta with json.dumps(data). | Verify that fallback is correct.

line 372 | low | _parse_typed_event for event_type in ('bash','command','shell','command_execution') uses int(data.get('exit_code') or 0); if exit_code is 0, 'or 0' returns 0; if exit_code is None, returns 0; if exit_code is 0 as int, works. | Fine.
line 381 | low | _parse_typed_event default returns AgentMessage with role='system'; comment says lifecycle events aren't misrepresented as text generated by model. | Verified.
line 384 | low | approve and reject raise NotImplementedError; comment says 'one-shot CLI profiles do not expose a portable approval protocol'. | Uncheckable: protocol not defined in chunk.
line 393 | low | terminate method stops process and cancels stderr_task if not done after 1s timeout. | Cancelling may leave stderr incomplete.

handoff.purpose: Contains stream method for reading subprocess output, line parsing, event construction, and session control methods (approve, reject, interrupt, terminate).

symbols.name: stream
symbols.note: Async generator that yields AgentEvent objects from subprocess stdout. Publishes SessionStarted, then reads lines until EOF or timeout, publishing parsed events. Finally publishes SessionEnded.

symbols.name: _parse_line
symbols.note: Parses a single line from subprocess stdout. If output_format is 'text', returns TextDelta. Otherwise tries JSON parse; if fails, returns TextDelta. If JSON dict, dispatches to _parse_typed_event or constructs AgentMessage/TextDelta based on keys.

symbols.name: _parse_typed_event
symbols.note: Parses a typed event dict based on event_type string. Handles text, assistant, result, tool_use, tool_result, bash, message, and default lifecycle events.

symbols.name: approve
symbols.note: Raises NotImplementedError. Intended for approval protocol but not implemented.

symbols.name: reject
symbols.note: Raises NotImplementedError. Intended for approval protocol but not implemented.

symbols.name: interrupt
symbols.note: Sends SIGINT to the subprocess of a session if it is still running.

symbols.name: _stop_process
symbols.note: Static method that terminates a subprocess. First tries terminate, then kill after 5s timeout. Handles ProcessLookupError and OSError.

symbols.name: terminate
symbols.note: Pops session from internal dicts, stops process, and awaits/cancels stderr_task.

claims.text: Lifecycle events are still observable, but aren't misrepresented as text generated by the model.
claims.why: The default return in _parse_typed_event returns AgentMessage(content=json.dumps(data), role='system'), which explicitly sets role to 'system', not 'assistant' or 'user', thus not misrepresenting as model-generated text.

claims.text: one-shot CLI profiles do not expose a portable approval protocol
claims.why: The comment explains why approve/reject raise NotImplementedError, but the claim about 'one-shot CLI profiles' is not verifiable from this chunk alone.

observations.what: stream method publishes SessionStarted before checking timeout; if timeout already expired, SessionStarted is published but then TimeoutError is raised.
SessionEnded truncates stderr to last 4000 characters, which may lose important error context.

In _parse_typed_event, for event_type 'assistant', if message.content is a list of text blocks, they are concatenated; otherwise falls back to json.dumps(data). This may produce unexpected output for non-standard formats.
approve and reject raise NotImplementedError, which will crash if called. The comment says they are not needed for one-shot CLI profiles, but there is no guard to prevent calling them.
terminate method cancels stderr_task after 1s timeout, which may leave stderr incomplete.
